stories.headline: Taiwan raids Super Micro offices, widening Nvidia AI-chip smuggling probe

key_facts.fact: Taiwanese government agencies raided Super Micro Computer's Taiwan offices and several local affiliates on Monday, June 29, deepening an investigation into the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China using the company's servers.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer and several of its local affiliates, deepening an investigation into the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China using the company's servers.

key_facts.fact: Twelve sites were raided Monday, including the homes of six people and the offices of Nasdaq-listed Super Micro Computer and Taiwan-listed firms Albatron Technology and Chief Telecom.
key_facts.excerpt: Twelve sites were raided on Monday as part of the probe... They included the homes of six people and offices of the companies they worked for - Nasdaq-listed Super Micro Computer and Taiwan-listed firms Albatron Technology and Chief Telecom.

key_facts.fact: Nine people are now under investigation, up from three previously, the head prosecutor of the Keelung Prosecutors Office told AFP.
key_facts.excerpt: Nine people are now under investigation, up from three previously, Huang Sheng, head prosecutor in the Keelung Prosecutors Office, told AFP.

key_facts.fact: Suspects are accused of forging documents to ship roughly 50 Super Micro servers containing advanced Nvidia chips to China, Macau and Hong Kong; some were cleared by Taiwan customs and sent to China via Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: They are accused of forging documents so they could ship roughly 50 servers made by Super Micro Computer to China. Some of the servers were cleared by Taiwan customs and sent to China via Japan.

key_facts.fact: Super Micro shares fell more than 9% on the news; the raids mark Taiwan's first formal crackdown on AI chip diversion after years of US pressure.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro shares fell more than nine percent on the news... The raid extends Taiwan's first formal crackdown on AI chip diversion, which began in May.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan does not currently treat AI chip exports to China as a crime; the only legal recourse is to charge suspected smugglers with violations of other existing local laws.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan does not currently treat AI chip exports to China as a crime... the only legal recourse through the island's courts is to charge suspected smugglers with violations of other, existing local laws.

stories.headline: Digital Realty buys Blackstone's stake in 3 Virginia data centers in $7.8B deal

key_facts.fact: Digital Realty agreed on June 29 to purchase Blackstone-affiliated funds' interest in three fully leased Northern Virginia data centers containing 288 megawatts of total IT capacity, at a gross value of $7.8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Digital Realty has agreed to purchase from Blackstone-affiliated funds... a stake in three fully leased data centers containing 288 megawatts of total IT capacity in Northern Virginia at a gross value of $7.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: Total consideration paid to Blackstone for its blended 64% equity interest is $3.5 billion, comprising $1.2 billion of cash and $2.3 billion in Digital Realty shares.
key_facts.excerpt: Total consideration paid to Blackstone for their blended 64% equity interest in the assets will be $3.5 billion, including $1.2 billion of cash and $2.3 billion in shares of Digital Realty.

key_facts.fact: The portfolio comprises two data centers in Manassas and one on the Digital Dulles campus in Sterling, each with 96 megawatts of IT capacity, all 100% leased to three distinct investment-grade hyperscale customers.
key_facts.excerpt: The portfolio comprises two data centers in Manassas and one on the Digital Dulles campus in Sterling, each with 96 megawatts of IT capacity, that are 100% leased to three distinct investment grade hyperscale customers.

key_facts.fact: Digital Realty is acquiring Blackstone's 80% interest in the two Manassas data centers and a 50% interest in the Sterling data center.
key_facts.excerpt: Digital Realty will acquire Blackstone's 80 per cent interest in two 96-megawatt data centers in Manassas, Virginia, and a 50 per cent interest in a 96-megawatt center in Sterling, Virginia.

key_facts.fact: The deal is supported by 15-year leases with a blended average AA- customer credit rating and 3.6% annual rent escalators, and was expected to close on June 30, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: supported by 15-year leases with a blended average AA- customer credit rating and 3.6% annual rent escalators... The purchase is expected to be completed on June 30, 2026.

stories.headline: Five Chinese tech firms launch $5.6B Hong Kong listings, led by Apple supplier Luxshare

key_facts.fact: Five Chinese technology and advanced manufacturing companies launched Hong Kong listings on Tuesday, June 30, to raise up to HK$44.1 billion ($5.6 billion), one of the busiest days for new share sales this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Five Chinese technology and advanced manufacturing companies launched Hong Kong listings on Tuesday to raise up to HK$44.1 billion ($5.6 billion), one of the busiest days for new share sales this year.

key_facts.fact: The biggest offering is Shenzhen-listed Apple supplier Luxshare Precision Industry, seeking up to HK$24.27 billion ($3.15 billion) by selling 383.5 million shares at a maximum HK$63.28 each, with final pricing on July 8 and trading from July 9.
key_facts.excerpt: The biggest of the five offerings is Shenzhen-listed Apple supplier Luxshare Precision Industry, looking to raise up to HK$24.27 billion ($3.15 billion)... Luxshare is selling 383.5 million shares at a maximum offer price of HK$63.28 apiece... The final price will be set on July 8, with trading set to commence the following day.

key_facts.fact: The five deals cover companies that make electronics, ceramic parts, chips, circuit-board tools and robots.
key_facts.excerpt: The five deals cover companies that make electronics, ceramic parts, chips, circuit-board tools and robots.

key_facts.fact: Nexchip Semiconductor, described as China's third-largest chip foundry behind SMIC and Hua Hong, is looking to raise up to HK$6.98 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexchip Semiconductor, China's third-largest chip foundry behind SMIC and Hua Hong Semiconductor, is looking to raise HK$6.98 billion.

key_facts.fact: The smallest deal is Rokae (Shandong) Robotics Group, selling 23 million shares at HK$38 each to raise about HK$875 million; the company makes industrial robots, collaborative robots and newer AI-linked robots.
key_facts.excerpt: Rokae (Shandong) Robotics Group, the smallest of the five deals, said it would sell 23 million shares at HK$38 each to raise about HK$875 million. The company makes industrial robots, collaborative robots that can work near people and newer AI-linked robots.

key_facts.fact: Hong Kong has seen $22.45 billion of new listings in the first half of 2026, up nearly 57% from a year earlier, the busiest start to the year in five years, per LSEG data.
key_facts.excerpt: There has been $22.45 billion worth of new listings in Hong Kong in the first half, up nearly 57% from a year earlier, making it the busiest start to the year in five years, according to LSEG data.

stories.headline: Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo again cut 2026 smartphone targets, some by up to 30%

key_facts.fact: Major Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo have told suppliers they will again cut shipment targets for 2026 -- some by up to 30% -- as rising costs and unprecedented component shortages weigh on the market, sources told Nikkei Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: Major Chinese smartphone makers including Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo have told suppliers they will again cut shipment targets for this year -- some by up to 30% -- as rising costs and unprecedented component shortages continue to weigh heavily on the market.

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi has lowered its internal shipment forecast to around 95 million smartphones, down from an earlier target of 135 million units and well below the 170 million devices it shipped in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Xiaomi has lowered its internal shipment forecast to around 95 million smartphones, down from an earlier target of 135 million units and well below the 170 million devices it shipped in 2025.

key_facts.fact: This marks the second round of downward revisions this year for the trio, following earlier cuts reported in January.
key_facts.excerpt: This marks the second round of downward revisions this year for the trio, following earlier cuts reported in January.

key_facts.fact: South China Morning Post indicated Xiaomi had reportedly reduced its 2026 shipment projection by 70 million units from a prior target of 180 million units, while Oppo cut by over 20% and Vivo by nearly 15%.
key_facts.excerpt: South China Morning Post indicated the scale of the slide for Xiaomi specifically, noting the company had reportedly reduced its 2026 shipment projections by 70 million units from a prior target of 180 million units, while Oppo and Vivo had separately decreased their shipment forecasts by over 20 percent and nearly 15 percent.

key_facts.excerpt: Reed Semiconductor announced an upsized, oversubscribed $100 million financing round with participation from leading global semiconductor companies.

key_facts.fact: The Warwick, Rhode Island-based company positions itself as a provider of turnkey power solutions for AI infrastructure, with materials emphasizing AI, data centers and high-performance computing power delivery.

key_facts.fact: Reed said the new capital will accelerate product development, expand market reach, and increase operating scale.
